title: Wanchain Cardano<->BNB bridge TreasuryCheck non-injective signed-message encoding
closed_reasons: Replacement Plutus V3 check script 8c027908... builds the signed digest as sha3_256(serialiseData(ConstrData ...)) and contains zero AppendByteString builtins; canonical CBOR is injective
Storeman GPK rotated in the reference GroupInfo (0335664e... at exploit -> 022af717... now); the real exploit signature verifies only under the old key
GroupInfo reference input is authenticated by the GroupInfoTokenCoin NFT (policy 1ddf09a9..., a script parameter), so a forged GroupInfo cannot substitute an attacker key
Every TCheckCoin (supply 63) sits at a check-script address; the treasury value validator requires exactly one TCheckCoin across inputs
No legacy-format (raw-concat) signature under the current GPK exists; the old V2 path has been dormant since block 13,703,937 (2026-07-21)
key_facts: Treasury addr1xyw0ksw... holds 218,156.077399 ADA + 11,837,345.212388 NIGHT + 30 CNTs in 306 UTxOs (block 14,152,985)
Treasury last moved block 14,048,512 / 2026-10-10 02:41:36 UTC; 14 withdrawals that day all used the new V3 script
The real exploit redeemer signature 322c4b49... verifies against sha3_256(170-byte raw concatenation) under GPK 0335664e... and fails under the rotated GPK 022af717...
Collision reproduced: amount/adaAmount (203001692164714,16) and (3097560000,1206800) both encode to the boundary bytes b8a103c0126a10; the V3 serialiseData digests differ
Exploited V2 script 485aa10343...: 15,989 B, AppendByteString=1, SerialiseData=1, Sha3_256=1; it does NOT self-bind to GroupInfo[TreasuryCheckVH]

Replacement V3 script 8c027908...: 6,501 B, AppendByteString=0, SerialiseData>=1, Sha3_256=1; parameterised with GroupInfo NFT 1ddf09a9..., Admin NFT 53cc8f42..., TCheckCoin 526d2460..., treasury 1cfb41dc...
Treasury value validator 1cfb41dc... source check is only: exactly one TCheckCoin across all inputs (traceIfFalse "hat")
TCheckCoin supply 63 across 6 script addresses: 14 at the exploited script 485aa1, 14 at the replacement 8c02, 35 at four older versions
Exploit tx 0a4861be... (block 13,702,781) moved 203,001,692.164714 NIGHT; four abnormal withdrawals totalled 515,206,545.426856 NIGHT
caveats: No Cardano node / Plutus CEK evaluator was available; no transaction was simulated on-chain
The V3 digest of the 2026-10-10 withdrawals was not reproduced byte-for-byte; the verdict rests on the builtin inventory (no AppendByteString) and the parameter/NFT construction
The V2 Haskell source is a recovered candidate from the DarkNavy artifact; it matches the deployed bytecode inventory and its reconstructed digest verifies the real on-chain signature

LATENT: the superseded V2 scripts are not self-disabling (they read the current GroupInfo and do not check their own hash). A single legacy-format signature under the current GPK would drain the treasury via the 14 stale TCheckCoin UTxOs at 485aa1. The public SDK (last commit 2026-05-28) still computes the legacy digest.
USD uses CoinGecko 2026-11-03; CNTs other than NIGHT are unpriced
P = $541,650.80 reflects storeman-threshold control of the treasury, not unprivileged extraction

Trigger resolved (TRIGGER-ANALYSIS.md): 24/24 storeman-signed Cardano txs since the GPK rotation are V3 serialiseData, 0 legacy, and 0 spends on the exploited V2 script; the legacy-signature trigger is not user-inducible (verdict b).
one_liner: External unprivileged attacker can extract ~$0 today: the replacement V3 check script uses sha3(serialiseData), the key was rotated, and 24/24 post-rotation signatures are V3 with zero legacy-format signatures — the $542k legacy-signature trigger requires a signer-side regression (verdict b), not a user action.

trigger_analysis.signer_format: V3 serialiseData (52/52 since the V3 migration)
trigger_analysis.verdict_text: only reachable via storeman/signing-flow mistake (legacy-format signature); not attacker-inducible
trigger_analysis.conditional_note: one leaked legacy signature drains the signed asset's entire treasury balance (NIGHT ~$502k); full ~$545.8k needs signatures for other assets
